drivingQuestion: What principle divides Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yishmael, and can each survive the verses — and how then is the mishna's 'one may slaughter with anything' to be explained?
outcomeNote: Both tannaitic positions survive the verses; Rabbi Yirmeya's dilemma is left teiku; Rabba's difficulty about the mishna's third phrase is settled by Rava's uniform re-reading, which displaces the explanations given in the two preceding units.

segments.he: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי? רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: בְּשַׂר תַּאֲוָה לָא אִיתְּסַר כְּלָל, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סָבַר: בְּשַׂר נְחִירָה לָא אִישְׁתְּרִי כְּלָל.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «With regard to what» principle «do they disagree?» The Gemara answers that «Rabbi Akiva holds:» The «meat of desire was not forbidden at all, and Rabbi Yishmael holds:» The «meat of stabbing was not permitted at all.»

segments.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב ״וְשָׁחַט אֶת בֶּן הַבָּקָר״, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַאי ״וְשָׁחַט״? קָדָשִׁים שָׁאנֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara asks a series of questions: «Granted, according to Rabbi Yishmael,» who holds that the meat of stabbing was forbidden in the wilderness, «that is» the meaning of that «which is written» with regard to the burnt offerings sacrificed in the Tabernacle: «“And he shall slaughter the young bull”» (Leviticus 1:5). «But according to Rabbi Akiva, what» is the meaning of: «“And he shall slaughter”?» Why would he slaughter it if stabbing is permitted? The Gemara answers: «Sacrificial» animals «are different,» as slaughter is required in that case. By contrast, there was no obligation to slaughter non-sacrificial animals to eat their meat.

segments.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב ״הֲצֹאן וּבָקָר יִשָּׁחֵט לָהֶם״, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַאי ״הֲצֹאן וּבָקָר יִשָּׁחֵט לָהֶם״? ״יִנָּחֵר לָהֶם״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! נְחִירָה שֶׁלָּהֶן זוֹ הִיא שְׁחִיטָתָן.
segments.en: «Granted, according to Rabbi Yishmael,» who holds that the meat of stabbing was forbidden in the wilderness, «that is» the meaning of that «which is written: “Will flocks and herds be slaughtered for them”» (Numbers 11:22), indicating that they slaughtered the animals in the wilderness. «But according to Rabbi Akiva, what» is the meaning of: «“Will flocks and herds be slaughtered for them”?» Ostensibly, the words: «Be stabbed for them, should have» been written. The Gemara answers: In the wilderness, «their stabbing is their slaughter.»

segments.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל – הַיְינוּ דִּתְנַן: הַשּׁוֹחֵט וְנִתְנַבְּלָה בְּיָדוֹ, וְהַנּוֹחֵר וְהַמְעַקֵּר – פָּטוּר מִלְּכַסּוֹת, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אַמַּאי פָּטוּר מִלְּכַסּוֹת?
segments.en: «Granted, according to Rabbi Yishmael, that is» the meaning of that «which we learned» in a mishna (85a) with regard to the mitzva of covering the blood of an undomesticated animal or a bird: «One who slaughters» an undomesticated animal and the slaughter is not valid «and it became an unslaughtered carcass by his hand, and one who stabs» an animal, «and one who rips» the simanim from their place before cutting them, invalidating the slaughter, is «exempt from covering» the blood. One must cover the blood of only an animal whose slaughter was valid. «But according to Rabbi Akiva, why is one exempt from covering» the blood of an animal that was stabbed, since in his opinion when they were commanded to cover blood, animals that were stabbed were permitted?
The Gemara answers: «Since» the meat of stabbing «was forbidden, it was forbidden,» and the halakhic status of stabbing is no longer that of slaughtering.

segments.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דְּאָמַר בְּשַׂר תַּאֲוָה לָא אִיתְּסַר כְּלָל – הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: ״אַךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵאָכֵל אֶת הַצְּבִי וְאֶת הָאַיָּל כֵּן תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ״, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, צְבִי וְאַיָּל גּוּפֵיהּ מִי הֲוֵי שְׁרֵי?
segments.en: «Granted, according to Rabbi Akiva, who says» that the «meat of desire was not forbidden at all, that is» the meaning of that «which is written» before they entered Eretz Yisrael: «“However, as the gazelle and as the deer is eaten, so shall you eat of it,» the pure and the impure may eat of it alike” (Deuteronomy 12:22). This means that just as it is permitted to eat the meat of a gazelle and a deer in the wilderness in a state of ritual impurity, so may you eat them when you enter Eretz Yisrael, although at that point it will be prohibited to stab them and eat their meat, as their meat will be permitted only through slaughter. «But according to Rabbi Yishmael,» who holds that the meat of desire was forbidden in the wilderness, «were the gazelle and the deer themselves permitted» in the wilderness? They are not brought as offerings.

segments.he: כִּי אֲסַר רַחֲמָנָא – בְּהֵמָה דְּחַזְיָא לְהַקְרָבָה, אֲבָל חַיָּה דְּלָא חַזְיָא לְהַקְרָבָה – לָא אֲסַר רַחֲמָנָא.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «When the Merciful One rendered» the meat of desire «forbidden,» that was specifically the meat of «a domesticated animal that is fit for sacrifice. But the Merciful One did not render forbidden undomesticated animals that are not fit for sacrifice.»

segments.he: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: אֵבְרֵי בְּשַׂר נְחִירָה שֶׁהִכְנִיסוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עִמָּהֶן לָאָרֶץ, מַהוּ?
segments.en: § «Rabbi Yirmeya raises a dilemma» according to the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, who says that the meat of stabbing was permitted in the wilderness: With regard to «the limbs of» the «meat of stabbing that the Jewish people took with them into Eretz» Yisrael, «what is» their halakhic status?

segments.he: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא בְּשֶׁבַע שֶׁכִּבְּשׁוּ – הַשְׁתָּא דָּבָר טָמֵא אִישְׁתְּרִי לְהוּ, דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבָתִּים מְלֵאִים כׇּל טוּב״, וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב: כֻּתְלֵי דַּחֲזִירֵי – בְּשַׂר נְחִירָה מִבַּעְיָא?
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «When?» With regard to what period does Rabbi Yirmeya raise his dilemma? «If we say» that the dilemma is «with regard to» the «seven» years during «which they conquered» the land, «now, non-kosher items were permitted for them» during that period, «as it is written:» “And it shall be, when the Lord your God shall bring you into the land that He swore to your fathers, «and houses full of all good things…»and you shall eat and be satisfied” (Deuteronomy 6:10–11), «and Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba says» that «Rav says: Cuts of pig» meat «[kotlei daḥazirei]» that they found in the houses were permitted for them; is it «necessary» to say that the «meat» from the «stabbing» of a kosher animal was permitted?

segments.he: אֶלָּא, לְאַחַר מִכָּאן. וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם בְּשֶׁבַע שֶׁכִּבְּשׁוּ, כִּי אִשְׁתְּרִי לְהוּ שָׁלָל שֶׁל גּוֹיִם – דִּידְהוּ לָא אִישְׁתְּרִי. תֵּיקוּ.
segments.en: «Rather,» Rabbi Yirmeya’s dilemma is with regard to the period «thereafter. And if you wish, say» instead: «Actually,» his dilemma is «with regard to» the «seven» years during «which they conquered» the land, as perhaps «when» the forbidden food «was permitted for them,» it was specifically food from «the spoils of gentiles,» but «their own» forbidden food «was not permitted.» The Gemara concludes: The dilemma «shall stand» unresolved.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבָּה: שַׁנֵּית ״הַכֹּל שׁוֹחֲטִין״ וּ״לְעוֹלָם שׁוֹחֲטִין״, ״בַּכֹּל שׁוֹחֲטִים״ – מַאי מְשַׁנֵּית לֵיהּ?
segments.en: § «Rabba says: You explained» the phrases in the mishna: «All slaughter, and: One may always slaughter.» In «what» way «do you explain» the phrase: «One may slaughter with any» item that cuts?

segments.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא, בֵּין בְּצוֹר בֵּין בִּזְכוּכִית בֵּין בִּקְרוּמִית שֶׁל קָנֶה, הָא דּוּמְיָא דְּהָנָךְ קָתָנֵי; אִי הָנָךְ בְּשׁוֹחֲטִין – הַאי נָמֵי בְּשׁוֹחֲטִין, וְאִי הָנָךְ בְּנִשְׁחָטִין – הַאי נָמֵי בְּנִשְׁחָטִין.
segments.en: «And if you would say» that it means: «Whether with a flint, or with glass» shards, «or with the stalk of a reed, but isn’t» this phrase «taught» in a manner «similar to those» other phrases in the mishna? «If these» phrases: All slaughter, and: One may always slaughter, are referring «to those that slaughter, this» phrase «too» is referring «to those that slaughter; and if those» phrases are referring «to those that are slaughtered, this» phrase «too» is referring «to those that are slaughtered.» The first two phrases in the mishna were explained as referring to the animals that are slaughtered. The first phrase was interpreted to include birds, and the second phrase was interpreted as referring to the halakha that meat may be eaten only through slaughter of the animal.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: ״הַכֹּל שׁוֹחֲטִין״, חֲדָא לְאֵתוֹיֵי כּוּתִי, וַחֲדָא לְאֵתוֹיֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשׁוּמָּד. ״לְעוֹלָם שׁוֹחֲטִין״ – בֵּין בַּיּוֹם בֵּין בַּלַּיְלָה, בֵּין בְּרֹאשׁ הַגָּג בֵּין בְּרֹאשׁ הַסְּפִינָה. ״בַּכֹּל שׁוֹחֲטִין״ – בֵּין בְּצוֹר, בֵּין בִּזְכוּכִית, בֵּין בִּקְרוּמִית שֶׁל קָנֶה.
segments.en: «Rather, Rava said» that the entire mishna is referring to those that slaughter. The initial phrase means «everyone [hakkol] slaughters.» Although an identical phrase was used in the first mishna (2a), both are necessary: «One is to include a Samaritan and one is to include a Jewish transgressor.» The second phrase: «One may always slaughter,» means «both during the day and at night, both on a rooftop and atop a ship,» and there is no concern that it will appear that he is slaughtering in an idolatrous manner to the hosts of heaven or to the god of the sea. The phrase: «One may slaughter with any» item that cuts, means: «Whether with a flint, or with glass» shards, «or with the stalk of a reed.»

moves.summary: asks what principle divides the two baraitot brought in the previous unit
moves.about: what principle divides Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yishmael in their two readings of Deuteronomy 12

moves.cueHe: רבי עקיבא סבר: בשר תאוה לא איתסר כלל
moves.summary: each tanna denies one of the two shifts: no prohibition of desire-meat, or no permission of stabbed meat
moves.about: attributing to Rabbi Akiva the premise that the meat of desire was never forbidden

moves.cueHe: בשלמא לרבי ישמעאל, היינו דכתיב ״ושחט את בן הבקר״
moves.summary: 'and he shall slaughter the young bull' presses against Rabbi Akiva
moves.about: why the Torah says 'and he shall slaughter' of the wilderness offerings if stabbing was then permitted

moves.summary: sacrificial animals always required slaughter, so the verse proves nothing about non-sacrificial meat
moves.about: sacrificial animals always required slaughter, so the verse says nothing about non-sacrificial meat

moves.cueHe: בשלמא לרבי ישמעאל, היינו דכתיב ״הצאן ובקר ישחט להם״
moves.summary: 'will flocks and herds be slaughtered for them' should have said 'be stabbed' on Rabbi Akiva's view
moves.about: why the wilderness verse says 'be slaughtered' rather than 'be stabbed' if stabbing was then the permitted mode

moves.summary: in the wilderness stabbing simply was their slaughter
moves.about: in the wilderness stabbing simply was their mode of slaughter, so the verse's word covers it

moves.cueHe: בשלמא לרבי ישמעאל, היינו דתנן: השוחט ונתנבלה בידו
moves.summary: the exemption of one who stabs from covering the blood presses against Rabbi Akiva
moves.about: why stabbing should exempt from covering the blood if, when the mitzva was given, stabbing still counted as slaughter

moves.summary: once stabbing was forbidden it lost the status of slaughter altogether
moves.about: once stabbing became forbidden it lost the status of slaughter for every purpose, covering of the blood included

moves.cueHe: בשלמא לרבי עקיבא, דאמר בשר תאוה לא איתסר כלל
moves.summary: the argument turns around: 'as the gazelle and the deer is eaten' presses against Rabbi Yishmael
moves.about: how the verse can compare eating to gazelle and deer if, on Rabbi Yishmael's view, even gazelle and deer were forbidden in the wilderness

moves.cueHe: כי אסר רחמנא – בהמה דחזיא להקרבה
moves.summary: only animals fit for the altar were covered by the wilderness prohibition
moves.about: the wilderness prohibition covered only domesticated animals fit for the altar, not undomesticated ones

moves.cueHe: בעי רבי ירמיה: אברי בשר נחירה שהכניסו ישראל עמהן לארץ, מהו?
moves.summary: Rabbi Yirmeya asks about limbs of stabbed meat carried into the land — a question that only arises if stabbing had been permitted
moves.about: the status of limbs of stabbed meat that the Israelites carried with them into the land

moves.summary: floats the seven years of conquest as the period in question
moves.about: the verse 'and houses full of all good things' as the licence for eating forbidden food during the conquest

moves.summary: knocks that down: even pig meat was permitted then, so stabbed kosher meat needs no asking
moves.about: rejecting the suggestion that the dilemma concerns the seven years of conquest, when even non-kosher food was permitted

moves.summary: asks which period the dilemma concerns
moves.about: which period the dilemma concerns — the seven years of conquest or afterward

moves.summary: the dilemma concerns the period after the conquest
moves.about: the dilemma concerns the period after the seven years of conquest

moves.summary: or it does concern the conquest years, since only gentile spoils were permitted
moves.about: an alternative: the dilemma does concern the conquest years, since only gentile spoils were permitted and not the Israelites' own forbidden food

moves.summary: the dilemma is left standing
moves.about: declaring Rabbi Yirmeya's dilemma about the limbs of stabbed meat insoluble

moves.cueHe: אמר רבה: שנית ״הכל שוחטין״ ו״לעולם שוחטין״
moves.summary: Rabba grants the explanations of the first two phrases and demands one for the third
moves.about: how the mishna's third phrase, 'one may slaughter with anything', can be explained once the first two have been explained as they were

moves.cueHe: וכי תימא, בין בצור בין בזכוכית בין בקרומית של קנה
moves.summary: floats the obvious answer — that the phrase names permitted implements
moves.about: the answer the interlocutor might give — that 'with anything' means with a flint, glass or a reed stalk

moves.summary: knocks it down: the third phrase must be parsed like the first two
moves.about: the third phrase must be parsed like the first two, and those were explained as speaking of what is slaughtered, not of the instrument

moves.summary: Rava re-reads all three phrases as speaking of those who slaughter, so the third may name implements after all
moves.about: resolving Rabba's difficulty by reading all three phrases of the mishna as speaking of those who slaughter

edges.cueHe: אמר רבה: שנית ״הכל שוחטין״ ו״לעולם שוחטין״, ״בכל שוחטים״ – מאי משנית ליה?
edges.about: how the mishna's third phrase, 'one may slaughter with anything', can be explained once the first two have been explained as they were

edges.cueHe: וכי תימא, בין בצור בין בזכוכית בין בקרומית של קנה
edges.about: the answer the interlocutor might give — that 'with anything' means with a flint, glass or a reed stalk

edges.cueHe: הא דומיא דהנך קתני
edges.about: the third phrase must be parsed like the first two, and those were explained as speaking of what is slaughtered, not of the instrument

edges.cueHe: אלא אמר רבא
edges.about: resolving Rabba's difficulty by reading all three phrases of the mishna as speaking of those who slaughter

edges.cueHe: ״לעולם שוחטין״ – בין ביום בין בלילה, בין בראש הגג בין בראש הספינה
edges.about: re-reading all three phrases uniformly: everyone slaughters, at any time and place, and with any cutting implement

edges.cueHe: חדא לאתויי כותי, וחדא לאתויי ישראל משומד
edges.about: what the repeated 'everyone slaughters' comes to include — a Samaritan in one place and a Jewish transgressor in the other

extras.about: whether the meat of desire was ever forbidden in the wilderness, or the meat of stabbing ever permitted there

extras.cueHe: רבי ישמעאל סבר: בשר נחירה לא אישתרי כלל
extras.about: attributing to Rabbi Yishmael the premise that the meat of stabbing was never permitted
the verse 'and he shall slaughter the young bull', which speaks of slaughter already in the wilderness
the verse 'will flocks and herds be slaughtered for them', spoken in the wilderness

extras.cueHe: דתנן: השוחט ונתנבלה בידו, והנוחר והמעקר – פטור מלכסות
extras.about: the mishna exempting one who stabs an animal from covering its blood

extras.cueHe: דאמר בשר תאוה לא איתסר כלל
extras.about: recalling Rabbi Akiva's premise that the meat of desire was never forbidden, before turning the next verse against Rabbi Yishmael

extras.cueHe: דכתיב: ״אך כאשר יאכל את הצבי ואת האיל כן תאכלנו״
extras.about: the verse 'however, as the gazelle and as the deer is eaten, so shall you eat of it'

extras.cueHe: ואמר רבי ירמיה בר אבא אמר רב: כתלי דחזירי
extras.about: Rav's ruling that even cuts of pig meat found in the houses were permitted during the conquest

extras.cueHe: ואמר רבי ירמיה בר אבא אמר רב
extras.about: adducing the ruling on cuts of pig meat as the a fortiori ground for rejecting the conquest-years reading
